messages:
sanjay: Quick heads-up — after the kernel-selector change in last deploy we're seeing a drop in prefix KV cache hit-rate for RAG-style chat workloads with long convo prefixes. filing here to track/debug.
olivia: Thanks. how big is the drop? rough numbers please.
maria: Profiling summary attached inline. baseline (pre-change) kv_prefix_hit 0.62, post-change 0.18 on sample workload A (30k convos).
maria: Detailed snapshot (relevant lines):
```
workload: rag-chat-longprefix
kernel: fused_attn_v5 -> matmul_stream_v2
batching: dynamic_max_tokens (old) -> greedy_pack_by_tokens (new)
requests: 30,412
kv_prefix_lookups: 120,456
kv_hits: 74,652 (0.619) -> 21,082 (0.175)
avg_prefix_len: 1.8k tokens
avg_latency_p50: 210ms -> 225ms
avg_latency_p95: 1.2s -> 1.6s
cpu/gpu utilization: +5%
```
kevin: interesting — hit-rate collapse suggests keying mismatch or different batching order changing prefix alignment. any evidence of key normalization regressing?
maria: I checked the key normalization unit tests, they passed. but runtime key construction path changed: we now canonicalize on tokenized subword sequence after kernel-aligned packing step. old path canonicalized earlier (before repacking). so keys can diverge for identical logical prefixes.
sanjay: so packing reorder can change token boundaries used for KV keys. that would explain chat vs completion diffs since chat prefixes are longer and more repetitive.
olivia: can we reproduce with a deterministic small sample and compare key strings?
maria: yes, ran a repro harness: same convo, two codepaths produce different keys for ~12% of requests. example diff: 
`old_key="conv|u123|tok: 0,1,2,..."` vs `new_key="conv|u123|tok:0,1,2... (packed@chunk2)"`
kevin: not surprising. behavior: earlier we canonicalized before merging system+history; new path merges then repacks which inserts boundary markers.
infra-bot: deploy 1779102178 by kevin: kernel-selector v0.21 -> v0.22, batching heuristics enable greedy_pack_by_tokens=true
sanjay: mitigation options: 1) revert packing change (fast), 2) normalize keys at a later stable point (medium), 3) best-effort cache compatibility layer that maps new keys to old keys using a lightweight fingerprint table (complex).
maria: quick experiment: enabling a compatibility flag maps 78% of previous misses back to hits in synthetic workload (small mem overhead). script: `kv.compat_map.enable=true`.
kevin: tradeoffs? memory and extra lookup latency?
maria: ~+8% memory, +1.5ms extra on miss path, but hit-rate recovers to ~0.56 and p95 latency improves back toward baseline.
olivia: sounds promising. can we prod this on dedicated staging (scale ~200 qps) before canary on prod?
sanjay: schedule: infra-runbook step 1: enable compat_map on staging, run 6h smoke, run hit-rate pk metric, confirm p95 <1.3s. if green, canary to 5% prod.
kevin: I'll open a tiny PR to gate compat_map behind feature flag and add a metric for compat_mapped_hits.
maria: adding test vectors and a small migration job to warm the compat map from historical keys. also adding a unit that asserts key parity for a set of samples.
infra-bot: ticket created #INF-2038 "prefix-key divergence post-kernel-pack" by kevin
sanjay: moving to follow-ups: (a) revisit kernel-selector ordering to avoid changing logical token boundaries if possible, (b) keep compat_map as short-term safety, (c) add a nightly job to sample keys and detect drift.
olivia: thanks — please ping here when PR and staging run start. :thumbsup:
